sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Mark the page, photograph it, let an agent process it
sections.para: Dinis loves books but never captured what he learned, because nobody processed the marks, so marking stopped. Reviewing his book on paper, he found the fix: photograph pen-marked pages and an agent reads, flags, redraws and writes them up. Thirteen pages gave 83 notes, and the book's new name.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Books, three moments, and the one that failed
sections.para: A book is the best medium and its inefficiencies are features. Reading means read, mark, process; the third never happened, so marking stopped. An agent now does it from a photograph, the title changed in the margins, and authors can get feedback this way.

sections.label: A book is my favourite medium
sections.line: Unconnected, unlinked, no undo: the book's features
sections.para: Dinis buys many books because a book suits him better than a screen: focus, no links, no undo. He learns in graphs and connections, and books are where many start.

sections.label: The three moments of reading
sections.line: Without processing, marking was not worth its cost
sections.para: Reading, marking and processing are three moments. Processing took hours and never happened, so highlighting stopped, and sometimes reading did too, losing the ideas formed at the best moment. The notes on August's printed graphs books never reached the site.

sections.label: What happened today
sections.line: A pen, a phone, and an agent that asks
sections.para: Dinis marks the page, photographs it, and the journalist agent captures each note word for word, redraws the page, sketches the change and asks when unsure. Thirteen pages gave 83 notes and 7 uncertain readings, five confirmed that day.

sections.label: The name changed in the margins
sections.line: From ZX developer to ZX founder, in pen
sections.para: Page 4 asks whether ZX founder is a better name; page 8 says 'ZX FOUNDER? :)'; page 10 says it should be about the reader. The same day the title became Generation ZX Founders (GenAI Edition), with other notes becoming decisions too.

sections.label: What I would like to do with every book
sections.line: The workflow for every book, paper and magazine
sections.para: Read with a pen, photograph later, and a Claude session captures, writes up and connects the notes so they can be found again: focus while reading, hyperlinks afterwards.

sections.label: And what an author would get
sections.line: Authors get the reader's thinking, unpackaged
sections.para: Reviewers can mark pages or record a memo and skip the third step; the agent packages it, so feedback no longer dies in the margin. The book's site wrote up the reviewers' side.

sections.label: This is the crude version
sections.line: Already valuable, before any tool exists
sections.para: A phone camera, a chat and a site that keeps the record are enough today. New model capabilities open doors like this, found only by using them.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Three batches, imperfect reading, one reader
sections.para: The counts cover 13 of 168 pages. Seven readings were uncertain and flagged. The workflow is a day old and untested on other handwriting; it is not a tool.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: A memo and the book site's review records
sections.para: Dinis's memo of 19 October 2026, the book site's RC2 on paper records and drawings, its paper-that-talks-both-ways article and decisions 016, 017 and 019.
